title: The Strategy That Thrives When Markets Panic - Systematic Investor - Ep.403

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/The Strategy That Thrives When Markets Panic - Systematic Investor - Ep.403.docx

speakers: Marat Molyboga (CRO and director of research, Efficient Capital Management)
summary:
Systematic Investor 403: June 2026 CTA update (May small gains, equities and energy trends after Iran shock, hard fixed income), Molyboga's views on manager access and behavioural mistakes, and Kaminski's paper on geopolitical risk and managed futures.
Geopolitical risk spikes precede inflation, hurt equities and bonds, and trend earns positive returns mainly via commodities and bonds; short-term trend adds value only with execution investment.
Also: mean-variance optimisation fails, equal risk plus vol targeting preferred, QIS overfit.

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: the best way to understand this asset class is in terms of the risk mitigation framework introduced by Makita
claims.claim: Makita's risk mitigation framework treats growth as the main driver of institutional risk and uses first responders (tail risk, long volatility) for sudden 10-15% drops, second responders (trend) for quarters-to-years dislocations, and diversifiers for uncorrelated return.
claims.conditions: trend disappoints in short, sharp selloffs
claims.testable: partly - classify strategies by response horizon

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: the AUM of happy investors and managed futures is still relatively small when we look at relative to other hedge fun strategies
claims.claim: The gap between benefits and AUM exists because investors misunderstand trend's role, make common mistakes, and use poor access (three obstacles).

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: performance chasing at both manager level as well as the industry level
claims.claim: Chasing recent best CTAs (e.g. top SG constituents) yields poor results because of low performance persistence; investors also pile in after crises and deallocate before the next one.
claims.testable: yes - top-N past performers forward returns

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: on any given year there's a pretty significant return dispersion between the best and the worst manager in the Saken CTA index and if you look at 2022 that return dispersion was around 80%
claims.claim: Return dispersion across CTAs is large (about 80% in 2022; one manager lost over 30% while the asset class gained 20%), so a diversified multi-manager approach with equal risk allocation and volatility targeting gives more consistent crisis alpha.

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: managed accounts allow scaling high higher sharp ratio portfolios up to accomplish high returns at the desired level of volatility
claims.claim: Managed accounts let investors scale a high-Sharpe multi-manager CTA portfolio to a desired volatility, unlike funds of hedge funds that cannot scale returns up.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: approximately right and precise as opposed to precisely wrong
claims.claim: CTAs seek approximately right solutions and well-thought-out decisions rather than precise but wrong complex formulas.

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: QS strategies, banks typically offer hundreds or maybe even thousands of strategies and they let you pick any one of them at the same time. The reputation is not on the line
claims.claim: Bank QIS strategies are more prone to overfitting than managed products because the issuer does not stake reputation on one strategy and offers many backtested ones.
claims.testable: yes - compare QIS live vs backtest

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: I call minus optimization a beautiful theory with ugly results
claims.claim: Mean-variance optimisation depends on forecasts of returns and covariances, so out-of-sample results are poor and weights unstable; equal risk allocation with tweaks for clusters is more promising.
claims.testable: yes - compare MVO vs equal risk out of sample

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: you can also diversify it across the dimension of time
claims.claim: Volatility targeting at portfolio level diversifies bets across time, further improving performance beyond equal risk allocation across managers.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: uncertainty in finance is too high for the complexity and the precision that we have to estimate a lot of these things
claims.claim: The 1/N paper shows estimation error makes complex portfolio choice fail; focus on what can be estimated (correlations a little, volatility reasonably) and use with caution.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: when we have higher geopolitical risk, there is a heightened perception of disastrous outcomes
claims.claim: Geopolitical risk (press-mention based index, Caldara-Iacoviello) raises perceived disaster risk, risk aversion and lowers consumer confidence, reducing growth; the dataset is granular by country and by threat versus realised event.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: geopolitical risk and increases in geopolitical risk is often followed by an increase in inflation
claims.claim: Historical studies find rises in geopolitical risk are followed by higher inflation for two to three years, with lower growth, supply disruptions, military spending, money growth and less trade.
claims.testable: yes - long history of GPR and CPI

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: But to me, it's not really obvious why trend would perform so well during periods of high geopolitical risk
claims.claim: The geopolitical risk to inflation link is a candidate explanation for why trend performs during geopolitical stress.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: geopolitical risk is funny. It's not very stationary, right? Like it's low and then it blows up
claims.claim: Geopolitical risk is non-stationary (jumps), so the study used the biggest increases and decreases of the index to sort months and examine asset returns.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: be spiking oftentimes during those times like um and the US dollar was generally up for the last 25 years
claims.claim: In months of the largest geopolitical risk increases over the last 25 years equities and bonds fell, energy spiked and the US dollar rose, consistent with an inflation shock.
claims.indicator: GPR index spikes and asset returns
claims.direction: equities down, bonds down, energy up, dollar up

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: managed futures tended to have very positive returns during higher geopolitical risk

claims.conditions: gains from commodities and fixed income, not equities

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: commodities is a place where we feel that pain during a geopolitical because it's something we all share
claims.claim: Geopolitical shocks cause supply and demand shocks, especially commodities; fixed income is vulnerable to inflation shocks; equities depend on whether growth is hit, which has not happened in this episode; trend adapts to a changing macro environment.
claims.indicator: commodity, bond, currency contributions to trend
claims.direction: commodity trend gains, bond trend gains if short

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: gibbleical risk causes inflation and inflation causes most of the markets tend to be profitable for trend
claims.claim: In high inflation commodities trend up and bonds fall, so geopolitical risk through inflation creates profitable trends.
claims.testable: yes - trend returns in high-inflation regimes

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: there were two strategies that stood out. One was lonely commodities and the second one was um trend following
claims.claim: In high-inflation historical periods stocks and bonds were mixed and negatively correlated 60/40 assumptions failed; long commodities and trend following stood out, so don't over-rely on 30-40 years of 60/40 history.
claims.indicator: 60/40, long commodities, trend in high inflation

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: short-term trend is able to increase the long-term performance of trend following strategies. So if you add them to long-term trend, medium trend, short-term trend improves long-term performance without sacrificing crisis alpha

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: the results are extremely sensitive
claims.claim: The benefit of short-term trend is very sensitive to transaction costs and market impact and disappears without investment in execution infrastructure (colocation, specialised algos).
claims.indicator: transaction cost sensitivity of short-term trend

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: those kind of strategies have not really done so well in the last 5 years or so
claims.claim: Short-term and long-volatility strategies, which gained after COVID, did not perform well in 2022 or the last five years versus long-term trend, possibly because recent crises (V-shaped, like Liberation Day) are too short for short-term models while slow trend does not blink.
claims.indicator: short-term trend and long-vol performance since 2020
claims.conditions: fails when crises are V-shaped or too short
claims.testable: partly - short vs long trend since 2020

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: the more different managers are from being long-term trend following, the higher their mortality is going to be
claims.claim: Managers more different from long-term trend (short-term, diversifying) have higher mortality, so good managers are hard to find and diversifying strategies hardest, though portfolios benefit when used.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the old days when a market opened higher it usually finished higher like 64% of the time and now he says it's like 56% or 58%
claims.claim: Signal decay in short-term breakout: markets that open higher used to finish higher about 64% of the time and now 56-58%, a small change that matters a lot for short-term strategies.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski

claims.claim: Faster, more reactive trend helps in fast crises like COVID, and a toolkit with varying speeds is valuable; the term short-term trend is defined broadly and costs rise with speed.
claims.direction: fast trend gains in fast crises

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen

claims.claim: Wind and solar generated more electricity worldwide than natural gas for the first time (April 2026), an energy-mix shift that creates an alternative to gas-driven power and is a structural driver for energy trends.

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga

claims.claim: After the worst industry drawdown (June 2025) and a strong run-up since July 2025, investors are again discussing a larger managed futures allocation, a sign that allocator interest follows recent performance.

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: investors get so disappointed with CTAs where they don't perform great during the weekly market selloff but they're not designed for that
claims.claim: CTAs are second responders, not designed to profit from sharp weekly sell-offs, so investors who judge them on such episodes are disappointed unnecessarily; tail-risk and long-volatility first responders are the right tool for sudden 10-15% drops.
claims.indicator: trend returns in short sell-offs vs prolonged dislocations
claims.conditions: short, sharp equity drops versus drops lasting quarters to years

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you could even say that about multi-manager firms saying oh we take all these managers we do a back test and they look good together
claims.claim: The backtest-overfitting criticism made of QIS products applies equally to replication strategies, multi-manager portfolios built on backtests and individual CTAs, so what differentiates them is out-of-sample evidence and accountability, not the existence of a backtest.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen

claims.claim: In months of extreme geopolitical-risk moves equities were not a main contributor to managed futures returns, so the gains came from commodities and fixed income (inflation channel) and timing equities in these events is hard, as in the current conflict.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: most consistent sector or sectors um that seem to perform well during these uh crisis comes
claims.claim: Recollection (attributed uncertainly) that across true equity crises the most consistent trend contributor is the commodity sector, even though equity positions typically lose money.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: Since this is a monthly frequency, you know, you're not going to see trend being able to capture that tech bubble
claims.claim: Crisis-alpha and drawdown analyses depend on the time horizon: at monthly frequency trend cannot show gains from slow-building events like the tech bubble, so the geopolitical result only describes shocks that move prices within a month.
claims.testable: yes - re-run at quarterly or annual frequency

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: if if you are worried about geopolitical risk that commodity trend is actually going to help you a lot during those environments
claims.claim: Allocators worried about crises, inflation or geopolitical risk should hold diversified trend with meaningful commodity trend exposure, because commodity trend is the sleeve that helps most in geopolitical environments.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: this paper was a great road map of how to think about investing over the next three to five years
claims.claim: Because history rhymes and geopolitical-risk episodes have been followed by inflation, lower growth and different asset behaviour, Kaminski expects the next three to five years to look different and treats the literature as a roadmap for allocating to trend.
claims.testable: partly - depends on the historical analogue

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: if we make a case for an investor to diversify to maybe six to 10 managers that's huge huge success
claims.claim: A practical target for diversifying manager risk is six to ten trend managers instead of the usual one or two, which captures crisis alpha more consistently.

claims.conditions: investors with only one or two managers

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: research point of view uh we find that generally they end up losing money over time
claims.claim: In the host's internal research, basic trend models with short lookback periods end up losing money over time, so short-term trend following is not profitable in a pure sense.
claims.conditions: basic trend signals before costs and refinements

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: shorter term managers did very well and and I can't say whether they were following or whether they were just what I would consider kind of trading the expansion of volatility
claims.claim: Short-term managers' strong 2020 may have come from trading the expansion of volatility and exiting positions without waiting for the market to turn, not from trend following, which would explain why it was not repeated.

claims.speaker: Marat Molyboga
claims.quote: a lot of managers use some for example pattern recognition techniques to generate returns right so it's not just purely short-term trend
claims.claim: Short-term CTAs are not only running short-term trend: many use pattern recognition and must keep innovating because signals decay quickly, so their results are not a clean test of short-term trend.
